facts.fact: Tunisia's return to UNESCO's 2024 SDG 16.10.2 survey names law no. 22 of 24 March 2016 as its access to information guarantee, with information officers required in all public bodies.

Tunisia's return to UNESCO's 2024 SDG 16.10.2 survey says a national information commission oversees the law, and reports 7,347 appeals received in January-December 2023 and 6,375 requests received in 2021.
ARTICLE 19 says parliament adopted Organic Law No. 22 of 2016 on the right of access to information in March 2016.
ARTICLE 19 says the national access to information authority (INAI) was established in 2017.
ARTICLE 19 says the government ordered all INAI activities halted, its seat closed and its staff reassigned, effectively dissolving the authority.
Reporters sans frontières refers to Tunisia's organic law no. 22 of 2016 on access to information as the basis on which parliament could still renew the INAI council.
RSF says the government closed the INAI in early August 2025: its quorum was lost in 2024, its staff were detached and its seat shut, though the dissolution is not official.

note: Says the oversight body INAI was dissolved in August 2025; states nothing on the law's standing or on rules made under it.
